spec.description: GreenLAG pipe lagging has a noise barrier with a microcellular structure designed to contain intrusive noise generated by the turbulent flow of liquids through pipes, fittings and ductwork break-out [3]. It incorporates a patented visco-elastic acoustic barrier using QuietWave technology bonded to a 15mm or 25mm solid foam decoupling layer and an outer durable aluminium foil facing [3]. Engineered for multi-storey residential, commercial and industrial buildings, it is the thinnest and lightest NCC-compliant acoustic pipe lagging on the Australian market [3].
features: Improved vibration damping with microcellular noise barrier and solid foam layer [3]
Reduced installation time resulting from flexibility and resilience [3]
Exceeds the acoustic requirements of the National Construction Code of Australia (NCC) [3]
Tough and tear-resistant yet easily cut and shaped [3]
Patented visco-elastic acoustic barrier using QuietWave technology [3]
Low VOCs (less than required for Green Star rating of 0.5mg) [3]
Flat foam GreenLAG is thinnest and lighter NCC compliant acoustic pipe lagging [3]
Cost effective with a saving of 12.7% compared to convoluted foam equivalent [3]
Proudly designed and manufactured in Australia [3]
applications: valves in multi-storey residential, commercial and industrial buildings [3]
spec.fire: Meets all fire codes set out in the National Construction Code (NCC) for waste water pipes [3]
spec.compliance: Exceeds NCC 2019 / NCC 2022 Ref. F5.6 (habitable and non-habitable room requirements); Green Star compliant [3]
spec.sustainability: Low VOCs (less than 0.5mg Green Star threshold); Non-toxic; Australian Made licensed [3]
install: Measure pipe outside diameter and cut GreenLAG to size allowing for 50mm overlaps [3]
Ensure foam decoupling layer faces inward directly against the pipe surface [3]
Wrap GreenLAG tightly around the pipe, elbow, branch or ductwork [3]
Overlap all longitudinal joints by a minimum of 50mm [3]
Seal all longitudinal and circumferential joints with reinforced aluminium foil tape [3]
Secure lagging with cable ties or tape at 200-300mm centres and at all joints [3]
Ensure complete coverage around pipe brackets, bends and penetrations with no acoustic flanking gaps [3]
selection_checklist: Confirm pipe application (habitable room requiring Rw+Ctr 40 vs non-habitable requiring Rw+Ctr 25) [3]
Confirm pipe diameter and total lineal meterage required [3]
Select foam thickness (18mm total thickness / 15mm foam vs 25mm foam) [3]
Check ceiling void / cavity clearance around pipework [3]
Ensure adequate supply of reinforced aluminium tape and cable ties [3]
limitations: Foam decoupling layer must always face the pipe surface [3]
All overlaps and penetrations must be fully sealed to prevent acoustic flanking [3]

problem_keywords: meeting NCC F5.6 pipe acoustic code
use_cases: lagging PVC soil and waste water pipes above plasterboard ceilings in multi-storey apartments
wrapping hydraulic pipes, valves and fan housings in commercial risers
insulating rainwater downpipes running through habitable rooms to exceed NCC Rw+Ctr 40 requirements
damping general noise breakout from air conditioning ductwork
not_for: high temperature steam pipe insulation without thermal insulation barrier
retrieval.rag_summary: Acoustica GreenLAG (Acoustica GL) is an ultra-thin, lightweight acoustic pipe lagging engineered to silence breakout noise from liquid flow in hydraulic, waste, and stormwater pipes. Constructed with a patented QuietWave visco-elastic microcellular acoustic barrier bonded to a 15mm or 25mm decoupling foam layer and reinforced aluminium foil outer face, it comfortably exceeds NCC acoustic requirements (Rw+Ctr 40 for habitable rooms and Rw+Ctr 25 for non-habitable rooms). Designed and manufactured in Australia with low VOC emissions, it wraps tightly around pipes, elbows, and ductwork to stop intrusive flushing and turbulent flow sounds in residential and commercial buildings.
